technique: Styled to look like clay/felt stop-motion (fibrous knit-sweater texture on the woman, matte clay-like skin and visible sculpted seams on the man's long nose and blocky black-suit torso), but the motion across all 14 periodic frames (~1s apart, static locked-off camera, 13.76s total) is continuously interpolated with no repeated/held frames, no set jitter, and no fingerprint/tool-mark micro-texture changing between frames the way handled armatures typically show. This reads as 3D CGI (or AI-generated video) built with a stop-motion/claymation shader rather than photographed physical puppets. Minor cross-frame inconsistencies in prop/limb geometry (e.g. the man's glasses and hand shift slightly in place/shape frame to frame beyond what a rigid puppet rig would allow) further suggest AI-assisted or CG generation rather than true stop-motion photography — flagging this as an uncertain read given only periodic (not per-frame) sampling.
facial_animation_notes: The woman's mouth cycles through multiple distinct open/closed viseme shapes (rounded 'O' on cup-sip poses, wider open shapes on dialogue words like 'UP.', 'YOU'VE', 'EVERY') that track smoothly with the burned-in captions. Her brow and upper eyelids sag into a consistent 'unimpressed/deadpan' set pose that barely varies, while the man's brows and eye-white size shift more, popping wider on words like 'DON'T' and 'ARE' to sell surprise/annoyance. No harsh frame-to-frame pops in mouth shape are visible; transitions look blended rather than stepped.
eye_and_blink_notes: No blink was caught in any of the 14 periodic samples — both characters keep eyes wide open throughout, with the woman's gaze drooping toward half-lidded 'tired' eyes and the man's eyes staying round and alert. Since periodic frames are roughly 1 second apart, any blinks would likely fall between samples, so blink frequency/style can't be confirmed from this evidence, only that eyes are rarely if ever shown closed.
head_movement_notes: Both heads stay close to a fixed base orientation for almost the entire sampled range — the woman's head has only a very slight downward/forward tilt toward her teacup, and the man's head shows a small tilt-and-turn when he reaches up to a cabinet handle (periodic-4 through periodic-10) before returning to a level, slightly quizzical tilt by the final frames. No large turns, nods, or camera-relative repositioning of the heads is visible across the sampled frames.
gesture_notes: The woman performs one continuous, smoothly staged action across nearly all sampled frames: lifting a teacup from saucer height to her lips and sipping, with the hand-to-mouth arc visibly progressing in small increments frame to frame rather than jumping between poses. The man performs a background task (loading a dishwasher, then reaching up to stack plates in a cabinet and gripping the cabinet handle) with his free hand gesturing open/emphatic while he talks, arm fully extended overhead in periodic-9/10.
idle_motion_notes: The camera is completely locked off across all sampled frames — no dolly, pan, or handheld drift. Idle secondary motion is minimal: the woman's torso stays essentially static aside from the arm driving the teacup, and the man's stance is likewise mostly locked, with his lower body (blocky black suit/legs) not shifting weight at all between frames while only his upper arms and head animate. Background elements (window light, cabinet cups, fruit bowl) show no incidental movement.
frame_rate_feel: Metadata reports 30fps, and the motion sampled here (teacup rising in small continuous steps, mouth shapes blending rather than snapping) feels closer to that full frame rate than to a stepped-down stop-motion cadence — there is no visible 'stutter' or held-pose chatter typical of animation shot on 2s or 3s holds. Overall impression is smooth/fluid motion dressed in a stop-motion-style skin rather than genuinely choppy stop-motion timing.
overall_animation_style_notes: The visual language borrows heavily from claymation/stop-motion aesthetics (textured wool sweater, sculpted clay-look skin, chunky simplified black-suit 'puppet' body for the man) inside a static single-set kitchen composition, but the underlying motion is smooth and continuous rather than frame-held, and word-by-word karaoke captions are burned in over the footage throughout. The combination of a stop-motion-styled look with non-stop-motion (smooth, camera-locked) motion timing is the most distinctive and slightly uncertain technical signature of this reel.
